findings.F1: The book loses mainly because it is short coins that drift upward. Its mean position is -0.186 and it is short on 30 % of bars. Its gain from the market's own rise is -0.022 % a day, more than its whole mean daily return of -0.011 %, so its timing is slightly positive (+0.011 % a day). Holding the coins earns +0.067 % to +0.155 % a day depending on the coin. Per case the total move is -0.13 % against a cost of 0.19 %, while the unusual move is +0.45 % (2.3 times the cost) but is eaten by a drift of -0.58 % in the short's direction.
findings.F2: The forecast's grading runs the wrong way, so the larger shorts do not fall more. The larger-forecast half minus the smaller half is -0.95 %. Active grid cases in the deepest 90-day-fall quartile end +0.16 % over 5 days, against -0.88 % in the second quartile. The four touch-strength quartiles show no order (-0.39 %, -0.14 %, +0.29 %, -0.34 %).
findings.F3: Shorts taken after a steep short fall lose the most.
findings.F4: Active grid cases fall further the less the coin has fallen over the past 20 days. The 20-day-return quartiles go from +0.69 % (mean -22 %) to -0.80 %, -0.45 % and -1.09 % (mean +6 %). The top quartile's 1.09 % short gain is 5.7 times the cost and above the coin's 5-day drift.
findings.F5: The losses sit in the years when the coins rose; the only year shorts paid was a falling one.
findings.F6: Trades lose more when the coin is more volatile: the top 20-day-volatility quartile (daily standard deviation 6.2 %) loses 1.84 % per trade (t -3.1), against +0.02 % to -0.76 % in the lower three.
findings.F7: The chained book falls 60 % at its deepest and has a fall of 33 % to 60 % in every year, ending 37 % below its start.

ideas.idea: When a coin's price falls back to a price where it turned up several times in the past 90 days while its 90-day return is negative, it tends to fall further over the next 5 days, and the higher its 20-day return at that retest (a calm return to the lows rather than a crash into them), the larger the further fall.
ideas.consequence: In a coin that has fallen over 90 days, a slow drift back to old lows would be a reason to sell, and a crash into them would not.
ideas.name: calm retest of lows fails

ideas.idea: When a coin's price falls back to a price where it turned up several times in the past 90 days after a sharp fall over the past 5 days, it tends to rise over the next 5 days, and the steeper that 5-day fall, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A crash into old lows would be a reason to buy, or at least to close a short, rather than to sell.
ideas.name: crash into lows rebounds
